title: Asparagus Soup
subtitle: Silky blended asparagus soup with a swirl of cream
excerpt: Fresh asparagus blended into a smooth, elegant soup with a light stock base and a swirl of cream. The tips are reserved and briefly blanched to serve on top. A classic British spring soup.

recipe.sourceNotes: British asparagus has a short season, typically from late April to mid-June (St George's Day to Midsummer's Day by tradition). Asparagus soup is one of the classic ways to use a glut when it is at its cheapest and most abundant. The recipe is simple: sweat the aromatics, add the trimmed asparagus stalks and stock, simmer briefly, blend smooth, and enrich with cream. The blanched tips reserved for serving are a traditional garnish that also extend the asparagus flavour across the bowl.

recipeTools.notes: Plus a blender or stick blender.

content.text: Snap off the woody base of each asparagus spear: hold both ends and bend until the spear snaps naturally. The snap point varies per spear and removes just the tough part. Cut the tips off and set aside for the garnish; use the stalks for the soup base. Blend until completely smooth for the silkiest result.
Cut the tips from the asparagus spears and set aside. Chop the stalks roughly.

Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the asparagus stalks and stock. Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes until the asparagus is completely tender.
Blend until completely smooth. Stir in the cream and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Blanch the reserved asparagus tips in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain. Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the tips. Add a drizzle of cream if wished.
